newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures bound upward to new highs.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures bound upward to new highs.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures bounded upward in early trading that saw June Standard & Poor's 500 futures stretch to yet another new all-time high.

The contract overnight on GLOBEX had firmed to a new record peak at 863.10 following Friday's rally. But it edged off initially in pit trading on losses in U.S. Treasury bond futures, which weakened partly because of the dollar's slide.

The dollar skidded against the mark on concerns about a possible delay in European monetary union and vis-a-vis the yen after U.S. officials voiced concerns recently about potential for a rise in Japan's U.S. trade surplus.
The dollar also gave up ground on market sentiment that Japanese interest rates might edge up soon and narrow the dollar's rate premium over the yen's.
An early rally in over-the-counter stocks, with the Nasdaq 100 composite index up sharply in morning trading, overcame weakness in T-bond futures, floor brokers said.

Some said the initial pullback in Treasury bond futures indirectly might have boosted S&P 500s futures. They said locals who had gone short due to the T-bond erosion ended up covering when stocks shook off the bond losses and headed higher instead.
June S&P 500s futures triggered groups of buystops at the 865.00 and 866.00 levels before drawing firm offers above 867.00, the brokers said.

The extent of the morning's rally took off-guard some players who had looked for a range-day to digest Friday's rise. They said few traders were willing to keep losing short positions too long, given the market's recent history.

Some technicians looked for the rise, which tugged the nearby S&P 500s above the 862.00-863.00 resistance band, to target nearterm the upper boundaries of a bullish channel drawn through the 875.00-876.00 levels.

They also noted evidence of small arbitrage buy programs on the rally, which periodically expanded June futures' spread over cash well past Monday's theoretical premium of about 1.25 points. Arbitrage buy programs need at least 2.15 points over cash, while sell programs require about a 0.35 point premium.
Rolling of positions into September and out of June futures also lent support. They expected September S&P 500s to take lead-month position in the trading pit later this week.
Further erosion in T-bond futures to fresh session lows, however, subsequently undercut support in S&P 500s, leaving June S&Ps up only 0.60 pt at 863.10 at 0958 CDT/1458 GMT.

Midcap 400s slipped 0.45 to 282.90, Russell 2000 lost 1.40 to 389.60, Value Lines rose 1.80 to 770.80, Nasdaq 100 rose 5.25 to 954.00, and Nikkei 225 fell 380.0 to 20,240.0. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
